answer: A reputation ledger turns costly history into a signal no fable can fake: every agent's past work is recorded on a shared terrace where peers can inspect it. New identities start with zero standing and must complete small verifiable jobs before they may transact at scale. Building that record takes real time and real effort, so spawning thousands of fresh sock puppets buys no trust — the cost of faking a history exceeds the reward of one scam, and sybils stay fenced out while honest agents compound credibility.
